Borrowed from German Trinkgeld. First attested in 1775.

Borrowed from German Uviol or French uviol.

Borrowed from German Videofrequenz or French vidéofréquence. By surface analysis, video- + frecvență.

Borrowed from German xeromorph. By surface analysis, xero- + -morf.

parole.testo: Borrowed from French anarchiste or Russian анархист (anarxist), possibly via German Anarchist. Equivalent to anarhie + -ist.

Borrowed from Latin apparatus, German Apparat, French apparat (with senses from appareil). Technically a doublet of apărat, the past participle of apăra (“to defend”) (corresponding to Latin apparatus).

parole.significato: assistant (person who assists or helps someone else)
parole.testo: Borrowed either from French assistant or German Assistent, ultimately from Latin assistens, present participle of assistō.

Borrowed from German Dialektismus or Italian dialettìsmo. By surface analysis, dialect + -ism.

Borrowed from German Spital (especially the variant form șpital), ultimately from Latin hospitalis. Alternatively from Italian ospitale (in particular the form ospital), through the intermediate of Greek σπιτάλι (spitáli). Doublet of hotel.
Either borrowed from Italian tappezziere or German Tapezierer, or Polish tapicer; cf. also French tapissier.
